scope: Read-only metadata and retained receipt audit for m2m.s.save_folder; no fixture content was read or hashed by this audit.

limitations: The 20.681-second sample is one read-only warm-cache timing of the legacy serial snapshot, not a repeated median.
The retained launcher timing phases are not included in this audit's summarized report; the 40.035-second subtraction includes both hashes and all other launcher overhead.
Do not infer that fixture hashing alone costs 41.362 seconds: cache state and phase timing differ, and two snapshot durations cannot be extrapolated from one sample.

per_case_io.reason: The retained JUnit and CTest logs contain case classifications, summary tallies, and aggregate elapsed time, but no per-case copy/read byte counters or phase timings. The separately retained folder-profile specification documents instrumentation but explicitly says it has not been built or run. This read-only task does not run that instrumentation.
per_case_io.output_bytes: Unknown per case. Existing diagnostic diff rows count changed/missing/extra files, not total output bytes.

likely_io_contention: The sweep itself is one CTest executable and serially handles the 98 cases, so CTest -j does not parallelize this critical path.

Each case recursively copies a project tree, invokes conversion and enumerates/reads files for comparison; the largest current corpus cases are ~25.7 MB and ~130 files, while historical manifest rows include two anomalous ~838 MB records absent from the current tree.

The two full fixture SHA snapshots read 1.87 GB each and compete with any concurrent CTest reads/copies for cache and storage bandwidth. Current evidence does not isolate that contention or attribute the sweep's 18.5 seconds to specific phases.
Sharding cases could increase simultaneous copy/compare traffic and make disk or antivirus contention worse; benchmark before assuming workers improve elapsed time.
